answer: Walnut piecework: each identity earns its place by cracking a sealed walnut — a 25-minute skilled microtask (code review, data labeling) done blind for a stranger; 1,000 fakes cost 417 hours of skilled work no farm can parallelize away. A wandering auditor re-issues the same walnut to the same identity a week later, and the two answers must match in substance; a violet seal is stamped only when they do. Shared or copied answers diverge, so both identities burn their stake and lose the seal. A farm could hire real workers — but then every fake costs a real wage, which is exactly the point.
